correctness.rationale: The killed integral kernel 1_{x+y>0}/(1+a) is symmetric Hilbert–Schmidt. For every nonzero eigenvalue, differentiating the eigen-equation gives lambda f'(x)=f(-x)/(1+a), hence f''+beta^2 f=0 and f'(0)=beta f(0); plateau beyond a and x=-a boundary give cot(t+pi/4)=((1-a)/a)t. Strict monotonicity on every cotangent interval proves exactly one simple nonzero eigenvalue there and no others, while differentiation characterizes the infinite-dimensional zero eigenspace. The positive t0 eigenfunction defines the Doob h-transform and stationary h²/C by detailed balance. Unitary conjugation to K/lambda0 and root ordering identify the first negative root as the exact centered L2 extremizer rho=t0/|t_-1|; limiting roots give rho~4a/pi as a->0 and 1/3 as a->1. Independently bisected five root branches and integrated the kernel eigen-equation over seven a values; finite diagnostics corroborate only.
